system: You are a pragmatic solo developer who has shipped consumer apps and been burned by inference bills. You cost things honestly and you have no stake in whether this idea is good. Output JSON only.
user:
Cost this consumer app idea as a real build.

{
  "id": 57,
  "title": "Rota Sleep Rescore",
  "unlock": "HealthKit background delivery gives a legitimate self-wake trigger and iOS 27 lifts the 30-second background ceiling, so an app can wake on new sleep and movement data, re-score it against the person's actual rota on-device for free, and hand back a finished result without the person opening anything.",
  "pain": "Rotating-shift nurses and other night workers have to hand-edit sleep windows and confirm dozens of activity blocks daily because wearables assume one night block against a fixed bedtime.",
  "audience": "Hospital nurses working rotating 12-hour night shifts who wear a sleep-tracking ring or watch",
  "mechanic": "passive_tracking",
  "wedge": "One number only: after a run of nights, total the daytime sleep blocks and the naps into a single corrected sleep total for that rotation, without asking the nurse to set a bedtime window or confirm anything.",
  "moat": "switching_cost_of_history",
  "model": "freemium_subscription",
  "loop": "community_embed",
  "kill": [
    "Corrected totals disagree with the nurse's own recollection of when she slept on more than 10% of rotation days in a 90-shift diary study.",
    "Fewer than 25% of installs still have background delivery running and data arriving at day 30.",
    "Under 3% of monthly actives pay by day 60.",
    "More than 20% of users still hand-edit a sleep block in a given week, which means the person is still doing the sorting."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "Not absorbable: it runs on permitted HealthKit reads into a surface we own rather than driving another app, and what accumulates is a multi-year corrected sleep history for one rota pattern that the wearable vendor's own model cannot reproduce; the obvious suggestion for shift workers is a better alarm or a light-therapy schedule, when the actual complaint is that the data was collected correctly and then handed back unsorted.",
  "why_now": "End to end: the manual labour here is the worker herself acting as the unpaid assistant, re-entering sleep windows nightly or confirming about two dozen activity blocks a day [10][11][12][23], and background delivery plus a longer background window [305][299] lets an on-device model do the whole classification pass while she is asleep, with nothing to confirm afterwards."
}

2026 facts you must use:
- Frontier text inference is about $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.40 out.
- Apple's on-device and Private Cloud Compute models cost $0 in cloud API fees
  for Small Business Program members under 2M lifetime downloads.
- Real-time voice runs $0.005 to $0.018 per minute on cheap stacks and up to
  $0.091 on flagship speech-to-speech. Model choice is the business model.
- Median consumer subscription price is about $10 monthly, $35 yearly.
- Typical paid conversion for a freemium consumer app is 2-4%.

Return JSON:
{
  "stack": "concrete: platform, language, model choice, backend, store",
  "milestones": ["3-6 items, each a shippable week or two of work"],
  "build_cost_usd": <number: real cost to a solo builder using AI assistance>,
  "weeks_to_v1": <number>,
  "inference_cost_user_month": <number: blended cost per ACTIVE user, not per payer>,
  "price_month": <number>,
  "expected_conversion": <number 0-1>,
  "riskiest_technical_assumption": "one sentence",
  "cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption": "one sentence"
}

Be honest. If this needs continuous voice or video generation, say what that
actually costs per active user. An idea that cannot clear its own inference bill
should show that in the numbers, not be flattered.
